title: Hawaii vs. Puerto Rico
text: Which Island Destination Is Better? Many people dream about visiting tropical islands. Two popular destinations are Hawaii and Puerto Rico. It is also farther from Guatemala. Puerto Rico is closer to Guatemala, so flights are often shorter. Puerto Rico is generally more Spanish-speaking than Hawaii. For many Guatemalans, Puerto Rico may feel more familiar because Spanish is the main language. In contrast, English is more common in Hawaii. When it comes to nature, Hawaii has some of the most spectacular landscapes in the world. Its volcanoes are more impressive than those of many other destinations. Puerto Rico, however, has one of the most beautiful rainforests in the Caribbean, El Yunque. Both destinations have excellent beaches. Some travelers think Hawaii has the best surfing beaches, while others prefer Puerto Rico because it is less expensive than Hawaii. In general, Hawaii is one of the most expensive vacation destinations in the United States. Food is another interesting difference. Puerto Rican food is spicier than Hawaiian food in some cases, while Hawaiian cuisine is more influenced by Asian cultures. In the end, neither destination is clearly better than the other. Hawaii may be the most exciting choice for travelers who love volcanoes and surfing. Puerto Rico may be the most convenient option for people who want a Caribbean experience in a Spanish-speaking environment.

title: The English Vowels
text:
Hello! My name is Carlos. Spanish is my native language. In Spanish, we have five vowel sounds, and we read the words exactly as we write them. But English is different. Here are some examples for you:
/ʌ/ (Short 'u'): This sound comes from the throat. It is very short and relaxed, like a quick Spanish "a".
Words: Cup, Bus, Sun, Run, Fun, Up.

/i:/ (Long 'e' / The smiling vowel): This is a long sound. You stretch your mouth into a smile when you say it.
Words: See, Meet, Tree.

/æ/ (Between 'a' and 'e'): To make this sound, open your mouth like you want to say "a", but try to say "e".
Words: Cat, Apple, Hat.

/ə/ (Schwa): This is the most common sound in English. It is a very short, quiet, and relaxed sound. You only hear it in syllables that do not have the stress or accent.
Words: About, Teacher, Listen.
